QT Imaging Issues Mid-Year 2026 CEO Letter to Shareholders
summary: NOVATO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- QT Imaging Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: QTI) (“QT Imaging” or the “Company”), a medical device…...
body_text: QT Imaging Issues Mid-Year 2026 CEO Letter to Shareholders August 18, 2026 8:30am EDT NOVATO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- QT Imaging Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: QTI) (“QT Imaging” or the “Company”), a medical device company dedicated to transforming breast health management through innovative, radiation-free imaging technology, today issued a mid-year 2026 letter to shareholders from its CEO, Dr. Raluca Dinu. The full text of the letter appears below and at this link which can be found on the QT Imaging website. Dear Fellow Shareholders, I am energized by QT Imaging’s many accomplishments so far in 2026, with impressive results by most any metric. Last week’s announcement of our second quarter financial results provides the catalyst for a review of the progress we’ve made, the foundation we’re building, and the priorities guiding us through the remainder of the year. Our mission is to transform breast health for every woman by addressing fundamental limitations in today’s breast imaging pathway. Mammography can miss cancers in dense breasts and requires compression, MRI can be expensive, time-consuming and uncomfortable, and conventional ultrasound remains operator-dependent, contributing to a fragmented workflow that can lead to recalls, patient anxiety and attrition. QT Imaging was built to address these challenges with a differentiated, FDA-cleared, three-dimensional breast imaging platform designed to provide accurate imaging for dense breasts without radiation, compression or contrast injection. By combining a more patient-friendly experience with quantitative, operator-independent imaging and a pathway toward AI-enabled biomarkers and precision diagnostics, we believe QT Imaging has the potential to simplify the breast imaging journey and advance a more personalized approach to breast health. Every milestone we report ultimately reflects progress toward a single objective: improving breast health. More than 12,000 women have now been imaged using Breast Acoustic CT™ imaging modality , providing growing real-world clinical experience with our technology. As we continue to expand commercial adoption, generate clinical evidence and advance our quantitative imaging platform, we remain focused on developing technology that can improve patient experience while providing physicians with meaningful, objective information to support breast health management. Executing Through a Challenging Market Environment The first half of 2026 was a period of meaningful progress for QT Imaging. We continued to execute against the priorities we established at the beginning of the year, strengthening our commercial, clinical, regulatory and operational foundation while advancing our long-term strategy. These accomplishments were achieved during a challenging period for growth-stage medical technology companies. While market conditions have remained difficult and investor sentiment across our sector has been subdued, we have remained focused on the areas within our control: disciplined execution, responsible capital allocation, continued innovation and expanding commercial adoption. The underlying opportunity we are pursuing has not changed. Women deserve better breast imaging, and physicians increasingly need objective, quantitative information to support more informed clinical decisions. At the same time, breast imaging continues to evolve toward more quantitative, data-driven and personalized approaches, creating opportunities for technologies that extend beyond conventional imaging. Against this backdrop, we entered 2026 with a clear objective: to strengthen every component required to support the broader adoption of the QT Imaging Platform. The progress outlined in this letter reflects steady execution toward that objective and continued investment in the commercial, clinical, scientific and operational capabilities we believe are essential for long-term success. Executing Our Commercial Strategy $14.0M +116% 28 12,000+ H1 REVENUE YOY SCANNERS SHIPPED WOMEN IMAGED The first half of 2026 marked another important step in our commercialization path. We generated $14.0 million in revenue, an increase of 116% over the first half of 2025, while shipping 28 Breast Acoustic CT scanners, double the number shipped during the same period last year. These results reflect continued commercial execution and growing market adoption as we expand our presence across the United States and internationally. As a reminder, QT Imaging generated no revenue in 2023, $4.9 million in revenue in 2024 and $18.9 million in 2025. With our 2026 revenue guidance of approximately $39 million, we believe this trajectory demonstrates the continued strong scaling of our commercial business. Yearly Revenue Fiscal Year Revenue Status FY 2023 $0.0M Actual FY 2024 $4.9M Actual FY 2025 $18.9M Actual FY 2026 ~$39.0M Guidance Equally important, we continued to strengthen the commercial infrastructure needed to support our next phase of growth. Under the leadership of our Chief Commercial Officer, Satrajit Misra, a seasoned medical imaging executive with three decades of industry experience, we expanded our direct U.S. commercial organization with the appointments of two experienced regional sales leaders. This expanded team strengthens our ability to engage directly with breast imaging centers, clinicians and enterprise health systems, while continuing to leverage our exclusive distribution partnership with NXC Imaging, a subsidiary of Canon Medical Systems USA. By combining established distribution infrastructure with expanded direct commercial and business development capabilities, we are building a scalable commercial model designed to deepen customer engagement, accelerate clinical adoption and installed-base growth, and support sustainable long-term revenue growth and margin expansion. Commercial Model Evolution Period Model Characteristics 2024–2026 Distributor Led Broad market coverage; capital efficient; rapid deployment 2027 and Beyond Hybrid Model Direct leads strategic accounts; premium economics/control; distributor supports service and financing Commercial strategy balances capital efficiency today with increasing control and margin expansion over time. Expanding Our International Strategy Internationally, we expanded our commercial infrastructure through experienced regional distribution partners with established market presence, local relationships and deep knowledge of their healthcare systems. Our distribution partnerships with Gulf Medical in Saudi Arabia and Al Naghi Medical in the United Arab Emirates, and sales agent partnership with Re-Invent Pharma in Pakistan provide a capital-efficient model for extending our commercial reach and supporting local market development. This partner-led approach enables QT Imaging to leverage established sales and service infrastructure while building the foundation for broader international adoption of our Breast Acoustic CT technology. While geopolitical developments have impacted commercial activities in parts of the Gulf region, we are beginning to see encouraging signs of renewed customer engagement, supported by our regulatory authorizations and distributor relationships. Our recent regulatory authorization in Israel, following regulatory clearance in Saudi Arabia and UAE, further expands our international commercial foundation as we continue to pursue additional opportunities. Together, these initiatives reflect the evolution of our commercialization strategy, from building market access to building commercial scale. By combining a differentiated technology platform with an expanding commercial organization, strong distribution partnerships and growing clinical engagement , we believe we are creating the foundation for long-term adoption of Breast Acoustic CT imaging modality and sustainable shareholder value. As we look toward 2027, our focus shifts from establishing commercial scale to accelerating adoption, expanding our installed base and increasingly leveraging the commercial infrastructure we have built to drive sustainable growth and margin expansion. Distribution Partners Partner Territory Agreement NXC Imaging (subsidiary of Canon Medical Systems) United States Distribution Agreement Gulf Medical Co., Ltd. Kingdom of Saudi Arabia Distribution Agreement Al Naghi Medical United Arab Emirates Distribution Agreement Re-Invent Pharma Pakistan Sales Agent Agreement Strengthening Our Financial Foundation The first half of 2026 was marked by several important milestones that strengthened both our financial position and our presence in the capital markets. During the second quarter, we successfully completed a $10 million underwritten public offering and extended the maturity of our senior secured term loan by two years, to March 31, 2029. Together, these actions enhanced our financial flexibility and reinforced our ability to execute our commercial, clinical and operational priorities while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation. Equally important, we strengthened our position in the public markets. Earlier this year, QT Imaging returned to the Nasdaq Capital Market , an important milestone that reflects the progress we have made in building the Company. We were also added to the Russell Microcap® Index , increasing our visibility within the institutional investment community and broadening awareness of QT Imaging among index-tracking funds and investors. Together, these milestones enhance our capital markets profile as we continue to execute our long-term growth strategy. As of August 7, 2026, we had approximately $14.2 million in cash and restricted cash , providing additional financial flexibility to execute our commercial, clinical and operational priorities. Together, these actions strengthened our balance sheet and our ability to invest in the next phase of growth while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation. We achieved these milestones during a challenging capital markets environment for growth-stage medical technology companies. By strengthening our balance sheet and expanding our presence in the public markets, we believe we are well positioned to invest in the initiatives that will create long-term value, including commercial expansion, clinical evidence generation, manufacturing scale, product innovation and the continued development of our quantitative breast imaging platform. Our objective remains to deploy capital thoughtfully, invest with discipline and build sustainable value for our shareholders. Expanding Our Regulatory and Quality Foundation We secured two FDA clearances that expanded the capabilities of the Breast Acoustic CT system , including an enhanced scanner configuration that improves posterior breast imaging coverage and software functionality supporting volumetric measurements for lesion doubling-time assessment. These enhancements reinforce QT Imaging’s strategy of continuously expanding the platform through innovation in both hardware and software. In July, we successfully completed our first routine FDA inspection with zero Form 483 observations . This is a truly meaningful accomplishment for our company. The inspection reviewed our quality management system and related processes. This outcome reflects the maturity of our quality systems, the preparation of our team, and our commitment to maintaining rigorous regulatory and quality standards as we scale. During the first half of 2026, we achieved important regulatory milestones that expanded the international availability of Breast Acoustic CT. We received regulatory clearance in Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates, and AMAR authorization from the Israeli Ministry of Health , further strengthening our presence across key international markets. These approvals reflect the growing recognition of our technology and establish a strong regulatory foundation for commercial expansion in the Gulf region and beyond. Regulatory Status by Market Market Status Saudi Arabia Regulatory authorization + Gulf Medical distribution UAE Regulatory authorization + Al Naghi Medical distribution Israel Regulatory authorization (AMAR) Europe CE Mark to address next Generating Clinical Evidence and Quantitative Differentiation Clinical evidence is essential to physician adoption, payer engagement, and the development of quantitative imaging biomarkers. Over the past few months, we continued to advance several complementary evidence programs. Mayo Clinic Study A prospective feasibility study evaluated QTscan in a supplemental imaging setting for 26 women at high lifetime risk of breast cancer. The study reported concordance between QTscan and MRI across 52 breasts and the identification by QTscan of all lesions considered suspicious on MRI. These pilot findings support the rationale for the second study to start in the next few months. Sunnybrook Breast Cancer Program An ongoing 100-patient clinical study is evaluating QTscan vs MRI to determine comparatively the sensitivity and specificity. Additionally, under our existing NIH contract, a clinical study evaluates advanced quantitative ultrasound findings in relation to treatment response in women receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy. This work is intended to assess the potential role of quantitative imaging in monitoring response earlier in the treatment course. Establishing the Foundation for Quantitative Breast Imaging During the first half of the year, we generated important scientific evidence demonstrating the reproducibility of Breast Acoustic CT’s quantitative imaging biomarkers through a multi-site repeatability and reproducibility study. By achieving less than 1% variability in Speed of Sound measurements across scanners, we demonstrated the consistency required for objective longitudinal monitoring and precision breast imaging. These results represent an important milestone in advancing breast imaging beyond visualization toward quantitative, data-driven clinical assessment. QT Imaging is also advancing a planned clinical study in collaboration with Rambam Health Care Campus in Israel , one of the country’s leading academic medical centers. The study is expected to evaluate Breast Acoustic CT image modality in women with hereditary risk for breast cancer, a population for whom effective longitudinal imaging is particularly important . The collaboration provides an opportunity to evaluate our radiation-free, compression-free, quantitative 3D imaging technology in a clinically important high-risk population and to generate additional evidence supporting its potential role in personalized breast health management. We are also advancing a prospective clinical study with Dr. Barry Roseman to evaluate our image modality in the diagnostic breast imaging pathway. The study will compare QTscan with established breast imaging modalities and, where available, pathology, with the goal of generating real-world clinical evidence supporting the diagnostic performance and broader adoption of our technology. Together, these programs are building a complementary body of evidence across diagnostic performance, high-risk populations, quantitative reproducibility and treatment-response monitoring—supporting our broader objective of establishing Breast Acoustic CT imaging modality as a clinically validated, quantitative breast imaging platform. Establishing the Path to U.S. Reimbursement & Adoption A critical milestone during the first half of 2026 was the American Medical Association’s approval of a Category III CPT® code for 3D quantitative transmission volumetric ultrasound tomography of the breast. The code was released on July 1, 2026, and becomes effective January 1, 2027. This dedicated code formally recognizes our service as distinct and provides a standardized mechanism for reporting, utilization tracking, and data collection. Importantly, the code creates the necessary framework to build clinical and health-economic evidence that can support future coverage decisions. As such, our reimbursement work is closely linked to our clinical strategy. We are engaging physicians, health systems, professional societies, and payers while expanding the evidence base needed to demonstrate where the QT Imaging Platform can deliver clinically meaningful information and value within breast health workflows. This is a multi-step process, but the CPT code represents a necessary and important step toward broader U.S. adoption. Our Platform Approach Innovation remains central to our strategy. The QT Imaging Breast Acoustic CT scanner generates true three-dimensional images and quantitative information about breast tissue without ionizing radiation or compression. During the first half of the year, we continued to improve the platform across hardware, image reconstruction, visualization, workflow, cloud connectivity, and AI-enabled analysis. Our collaboration with Olea Medical supports an advanced multi-modality viewing environment for QT Imaging data, including longitudinal review and comparisons with other breast imaging modalities. Our collaboration with Intelerad provides the secure cloud and PACS infrastructure needed for image management, clinical and research connectivity, and enterprise deployment of QT Imaging Precision Pathway. We are also continuing development of automated segmentation, tissue characterization, quantitative analysis, and AI-enabled workflow tools. These capabilities remain subject to appropriate development, validation, and regulatory pathways. Our objective is to preserve the long-term relevance of the installed scanner base while expanding the clinical and economic value of the QT Imaging Platform through software, analytics, and quantitative biomarkers. Business Model Hardware sale (scanner): upfront revenue SaaS platform: recurring revenue AI diagnostic layer: higher margin Hardware gets us in the door. Software builds the company. Strengthening Our Clinical and Scientific Leadership We continued to strengthen clinical expertise supporting the adoption of Breast Acoustic CT imaging modality through our Clinical Advisory Board. Dr. Mary W. Yamashita, Section Chief of Breast Imaging at USC’s Keck School of Medicine , brings deep expertise in breast imaging and clinical research and advises us on clinical interpretation standards, structured reporting and physician training. Dr. Barry Roseman, a fellowship-trained surgical oncologist and breast surgeon, completed his surgical residency at UCSF and his surgical oncology fellowship at MD Anderson Cancer Center and brings more than 25 years of experience in breast cancer diagnosis and care. Dr. John Tentinger, a Mayo Clinic-trained, board-certified radiologist, founder of Innovative Radiology and an early adopter of the Breast Acoustic CT scanner , brings hands-on experience integrating technology into clinical practice. Together, their complementary expertise across breast imaging, breast surgery and clinical practice is helping strengthen physician education, clinical implementation and broader adoption of our technology. We also strengthened our scientific leadership with the appointment of Dr. Julia Albright as Chief Science Officer . Dr. Albright brings more than three decades of leadership experience across medical imaging, healthcare technology, artificial intelligence and enterprise software. In this role, she is helping align our scientific strategy, product innovation, engineering and clinical programs as we advance the QT Imaging Platform. Mary W. Yamashita, MD USC KECK SCHOOL OF MEDICINE — BREAST IMAGING Section Chief of Breast Imaging at USC’s Keck School of Medicine, bringing deep expertise in breast imaging and clinical research. Advises on clinical interpretation standards, structured reporting and physician training. John Tentinger, MD MAYO CLINIC-TRAINED — CLINICAL ADOPTION / RADIOLOGY Board-certified radiologist, founder of Innovative Radiology and an early adopter of Breast Acoustic CT, bringing hands-on experience integrating the technology into clinical practice Barry Roseman, MD, FACS UCSF / MD ANDERSON — BREAST SURGICAL ONCOLOGY Fellowship-trained surgical oncologist and breast surgeon. Completed his surgical residency at UCSF and surgical oncology fellowship at MD Anderson, bringing 25+ years of experience in breast cancer diagnosis and care. Julia Albright, PhD CHIEF SCIENCE OFFICER Brings more than three decades of leadership experience across medical imaging, healthcare technology, artificial intelligence and enterprise software, helping align scientific strategy, product innovation and clinical programs. Expanding Manufacturing Capacity and Operational Readiness 22,000 2.5X ~55% SQ. FT. NEW HQ MORE OPERATIONAL SPACE LOWER LEASE COST / SQ. FT. During the second quarter, we entered into an agreement to relocate our headquarters and manufacturing operations to a new 22,000-square-foot facility in Petaluma, California, providing more than 2.5 times our current operational space while reducing lease cost per square foot by approximately 55%. The expanded facility represents an important investment in our next phase of commercial scale, providing increased manufacturing capacity, greater operating efficiency and the infrastructure needed to support a growing installed base and future production requirements. Importantly, we are expanding this capacity from a strong quality foundation, having successfully completed our first routine FDA inspection with zero Form 483 observations. Together, these investments in capacity, efficiency and quality position us to scale our operations with discipline as commercial demand grows. Expanded manufacturing capacity while improving operating efficiency 22,000-square-foot headquarters and manufacturing facility The expanded facility provides more than 2.5x the operational space of the current location while reducing lease cost per square foot by approximately 55% Successfully completed the Company’s first routine FDA inspection The inspection concluded with zero Form 483 observations, reflecting the strength of the Company’s Quality Management System and its focus on quality, compliance and manufacturing readiness Increasing Awareness of Patient-Centered Breast Imaging Creating a new category in breast imaging requires awareness among women, physicians, health systems, and policymakers. As part of our commitment to grassroots initiatives focused on breast health, I participated in two prestigious events hosted by The Shift. First was their inaugural Shiftmakers Gala celebrating women driving change, held at Harvard University in April and featuring actress and breast cancer survivor Olivia Munn. Then in June, I presented the Shiftmaker Award to tennis legend and two-time cancer survivor Martina Navratilova at the Sports Shiftmaker Awards ceremony during Wimbledon week in London. Through subsequent media coverage and social media posts, these events helped elevate the discussion around patient-centered imaging and the need for breast health technologies that can complement current approaches . We intend to keep awareness initiatives closely connected to our clinical, reimbursement, and commercial objectives. Multi-Generational Reach QTI is engaging with The Shift, a media platform reaching women across generations At Wimbledon and Harvard forums, Dr. Dinu joined leaders spotlighting breast density awareness The throughline: giving women greater choice in their screening journey Advocacy in Action Presented the inaugural Shiftmaker Award to tennis legend and cancer survivor Martina Navratilova Olivia Munn’s public story drove a 4,000% spike in risk-assessment testing Our Long-Term Opportunity Is Strengthening The underlying clinical and technological trends supporting our strategy continue to advance. National breast-density notification requirements have increased awareness of breast density, its association with breast cancer risk, and its effect on mammography sensitivity. This is elevating the discussion of supplemental imaging and more personalized breast health management. At the same time, medical imaging is moving toward more objective, quantitative, and longitudinal assessment. Cloud infrastructure and AI are increasingly being used to improve workflow and extract additional information from imaging data, while precision oncology is creating demand for reproducible biomarkers that may help characterize tissue and assess treatment response. QT Imaging is firmly established at the intersection of these trends. The QT Imaging Breast Acoustic CT scanner provides a differentiated imaging foundation, and QT Imaging Precision Pathway is being developed to extend that foundation through secure data management, collaboration, quantitative analysis, and future software applications. Priorities for the Second Half of 2026 Our priorities for the remainder of 2026 are to: # Priority 01 Accelerate commercial adoption by expanding our installed base through our integrated commercial strategy, combining established distribution partnerships with growing direct commercial, clinical and business development capabilities. 02 Strengthen the clinical and scientific foundation of Breast Acoustic CT imaging modality by expanding clinical evidence, advancing quantitative imaging biomarkers and deepening collaborations with leading academic and clinical institutions. 03 Expand global market access by advancing reimbursement in the United States, pursuing additional regulatory authorizations and commercial opportunities internationally, and supporting adoption across existing and new markets. 04 Advance the QT Imaging platform through continued innovation in image reconstruction, quantitative imaging, the QT Imaging Precision Pathway™ cloud platform and future AI-enabled clinical applications, supported by rigorous clinical validation and regulatory execution. 05 Scale the business with operational excellence by maintaining disciplined capital allocation while continuing to strengthen our manufacturing capacity, quality systems, operational infrastructure and organizational capabilities to support long-term growth. When we entered 2026, QT Imaging had an innovative FDA-cleared breast imaging technology and a clear vision for its future. Today, we are a stronger company. We have more than doubled revenue, strengthened our balance sheet, expanded our commercial organization, advanced reimbursement and regulatory pathways, generated important scientific evidence supporting our quantitative imaging platform, and invested in the manufacturing and operational infrastructure needed to support long-term growth. While we recognize that building a new category in breast imaging takes time, we believe we have made meaningful progress in establishing the commercial, clinical and operational foundation for sustainable growth. Our vision extends beyond introducing another breast imaging system. We are building a quantitative breast imaging platform that integrates advanced hardware, software, cloud infrastructure and, over time, AI-enabled clinical applications. We believe this platform has the potential to redefine how breast health is assessed by providing physicians with objective, reproducible and quantitative information to complement today’s imaging standards. As we look at the second half of 2026, and towards 2027, our priorities remain clear: accelerate commercial adoption, continue expanding our clinical and scientific evidence, broaden our regulatory and commercial presence globally, and execute with the operational discipline required to build a successful, enduring medical technology company. Thank you for your continued confidence and support. We remain deeply committed to our mission of improving breast health through innovation and look forward to sharing our continued progress as we execute our strategy and create long-term value for patients, providers and shareholders. Sincerely, Raluca Dinu, Ph.D CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER QT Imaging Holdings, Inc. August 18, 2026 About & Disclosures About QT Imaging QT Imaging Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: QTI) is a medical device company engaged in the research, development, and commercialization of innovative imaging systems that use low-frequency sound waves. title: Score Leads Automatically Based on Your ICP
summary: Surface scores every inbound lead against your Ideal Customer Profile automatically. Define your ICP in plain English and every lead gets classified as
body_text: Surface scores every inbound lead against your Ideal Customer Profile automatically. Define your ICP in plain English and every lead gets classified as Qualified, Disqualified, or Needs Review before it reaches sales. The Problem Leads come in and marketing sends them to sales. But no one knows which ones actually fit until a rep has already spent time researching, emailing, and getting on calls with leads that were never going to close. Traditional lead scoring doesn't solve this well. Legacy systems are rigid, take weeks to configure, and go stale the moment your ICP shifts or your form fields change. Most scoring models end up as a static point system that nobody trusts and everyone ignores. The result is that sales wastes hours on unqualified leads while qualified ones sit in the queue waiting for attention. How Intelligent Lead Scoring Works in Surface Surface takes a different approach. Instead of building complex point based rules, you describe your ideal customer in plain English. Go to Ideal Customer Profile in Surface, create your ICP definitions, and write descriptions like "Series A+ companies" or "YC backed company with 10+ employees and $1M+ ARR." That's it. Every lead that comes through your forms gets scored automatically against those definitions and classified into one of three categories: Classification What it means Qualified Lead matches your ICP, route to sales Disqualified Lead does not fit, filter out of the pipeline Needs Review Partial match, someone should take a look When your ICP evolves or new enrichment data comes in, scores update dynamically. You don't need to rebuild scoring rules every time your target market shifts. What Makes This Different From Traditional Lead Scoring Most lead scoring tools make you assign point values to individual attributes. Job title equals 10 points, company size over 500 equals 15 points, visited pricing page equals 5 points. You end up with a spreadsheet of rules that someone has to maintain and recalibrate constantly. Surface skips that entirely. You define what a good customer looks like in plain language and the scoring engine handles the rest. It uses enrichment data that Surface already captures (company size, industry, revenue, tech stack, seniority) to evaluate fit against your ICP definitions. No point systems. No manual recalibration. No scoring models that go stale after a quarter. Why This Matters Sales stops guessing which leads to prioritize. Marketing can measure how many qualified leads their campaigns actually produce. And your pipeline gets cleaner because unqualified leads are filtered before they ever reach a rep. The scoring runs on every lead automatically so there's no manual step between form submission and qualification. By the time a rep sees the lead, it already has a score and a classification attached. Frequently Asked Questions What is intelligent lead scoring? Intelligent lead scoring is the process of automatically evaluating inbound leads against your Ideal Customer Profile and classifying them as Qualified, Disqualified, or Needs Review. Unlike traditional point based scoring, it uses plain language ICP definitions instead of manual rule configuration. How do I define my ICP in Surface? Go to the Ideal Customer Profile section in Surface and describe your ideal customer in plain text. For example, "Series A+ companies" or "YC backed company with 10+ employees and $1M+ ARR." What data does Surface use to score leads? Surface uses enrichment data it already captures: company size, industry, estimated revenue, technology stack, job title, seniority level, and other data points appended during form fill. Do scores update when my ICP changes? Yes. When you update your ICP definitions or new enrichment data comes in, scores recalculate dynamically. No manual recalibration needed. How is this different from HubSpot or Salesforce lead scoring? Traditional CRM scoring requires you to build and maintain point based rules manually. Surface lets you define your ICP in plain English and scores leads automatically against those definitions. Scores update dynamically as your ICP evolves.

body_text: View All News Intrusion Launches 'Complete the Transformation' Shareholder Campaign Ahead of 2026 Annual Meeting August 6, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Stockholders as of June 30, 2026 are encouraged to review the proxy materials and vote promptly PLANO, TX / ACCESS Newswire / August 6, 2026 / Intrusion Inc. (NASDAQ:INTZ) ("Intrusion" or the "Company"), a leader in AI-powered cyberattack prevention and managed cybersecurity solutions, today announced the launch of its shareholder information campaign in advance of the Company's upcoming Annual Meeting of Shareholders. As part of the campaign, Chief Executive Officer Tony Scott and Chairman of the Board, Anthony LeVecchio have issued a Letter to Shareholders outlining the Company's strategic vision following the acquisition of VigilAigent and discussing why the Board of Directors unanimously recommends shareholders vote FOR Proposal 3. "Our industry is evolving rapidly, and we believe Intrusion must evolve with it," said Tony Scott, Chief Executive Officer of Intrusion. "The acquisition of VigilAigent represents an important step in our strategy to build a stronger cybersecurity platform with expanded recurring revenue, enhanced AI capabilities, broader commercial relationships, and improved operating leverage. While there is significant work ahead, we believe we have begun laying the foundation for the Company's next chapter." Anthony LeVecchio, Chairman of the Board of Directors, added, "The Board carefully evaluated this transaction, its strategic rationale, and its potential to strengthen Intrusion's long-term competitive position. After that review, the Board unanimously concluded that completing the transaction framework described in the Company's proxy statement is in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders. We encourage every shareholder to review the proxy materials carefully and make their voice heard by voting at the Annual Meeting." The shareholder letter describes management's perspective on the strategic rationale behind the acquisition and highlights progress since closing, including: Continued integration of the combined organizations while maintaining customer support and service continuity. More than $3 million in identified annualized operating cost synergies, as previously disclosed by management. Continued commercial momentum through publicly announced customer renewals, new business activity, and partner engagement. Expansion of Intrusion's strategic platform through enhanced AI capabilities, managed security expertise, proprietary threat intelligence, and broader commercial relationships. Management believes these initiatives strengthen the Company's long-term strategic positioning and support its objective of building a more scalable and resilient cybersecurity platform capable of delivering sustainable value for customers and shareholders. The Company also announced that, over the coming weeks, it intends to provide shareholders with additional information regarding the Company's strategy, integration progress, and the matters to be considered at the Annual Meeting. These communications are intended to help shareholders stay informed through factual updates and publicly disclosed information as they evaluate the proposals described in the definitive proxy statement. The Board of Directors unanimously recommends that shareholders vote FOR Proposal 3, which seeks the shareholder approval required under applicable Nasdaq rules to complete the transaction framework described in the Company's definitive proxy statement. Shareholders are encouraged to read the proxy materials carefully and submit their votes as early as possible. Every vote is important, regardless of the number of shares owned. Stockholders may vote using the instructions included with their proxy materials. Depending on how shares are held, voting may be available online, by telephone, or by mail. Stockholders who hold shares through more than one brokerage account may receive separate voting instructions for each account and should vote each eligible account. Built on years of gathering global internet intelligence and supporting government entities, this data forms the backbone of Intrusion's commercial solutions. title: StandardAero Signs Exclusive, Multi-Year Contract with Tanzania’s Precision Air For PW127M MRO Support
summary: Photo by ATR Aircraft / CC BY-SA 2.0
body_text: SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. – August 13, 2026 – StandardAero (NYSE: SARO), a leading independent pure-play provider of aerospace engine aftermarket services including engine maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) and engine component repair, has been selected by leading private Tanzanian airline operator Precision Air to provide MRO services for the Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127M turboprops powering its fleet of nine regional turboprop aircraft comprised of ATR 42-500/600 and ATR 72-500 platforms. This new contract extends Precision Air’s long-standing partnership with StandardAero. Under this exclusive, multi-year contract, StandardAero – the world’s largest independent Pratt & Whitney Canada authorized PW100 Designated Overhaul Facility (DOF) – will provide Precision Air with a range of PW127M MRO services from its overhaul locations in Summerside, Canada and Gonesse, France, supported by its service center location in Nairobi, Kenya. StandardAero has been serving the PW100 operator community for more than 40 years, having been appointed as the first independent MRO provider for the engine in 1984. Commenting on behalf of Precision Air, Christian Shirima, Head Of Maintenance stated: “We are delighted to renew our contract with StandardAero, which has been instrumental in attending to our engine needs, be it HSIs, overhauls, leased engines or unscheduled shop visits. Throughout our collaboration, StandardAero has demonstrated proven technical excellence and flexible support solutions. As Precision Air seeks to expand on its MRO capabilities on the ATR fleet, it will continue to integrate StandardAero’s engine programs into our maintenance planning and quality systems, enabling coordinated scheduling, shared technical data exchange and consistent compliance with regulatory requirements and the OEM’s directives. This renewed contract also complements the work of our Approved Training Organization. By aligning engine maintenance timelines and technical updates with our training curriculum, we ensure that technicians and flight crews receive the latest instruction on engine systems, troubleshooting and safety procedures. This coordinated approach reinforces best practices, improves maintenance proficiency, and enhances overall safety culture.” “StandardAero is truly delighted to extend our long-running relationship with Precision Air through this new contract,” commented Nasser Skalli Housseini, Regional Sales Director – Europe, Middle East & Africa for StandardAero. “We know how important it is for Precision Air to operate reliably for its customers, and we are committed to providing dependable engine services that support this objective. We look forward to continuing to provide Precision Air with responsive, reliable engine services for many years to come.” With more than 60 years of turboprop MRO experience, StandardAero is proven and trusted globally to provide reliable engine support tailored to an operator’s specific needs. StandardAero’s service offering on the PW100 family includes extensive component repair support, rental engine solutions, on-site field service, and engine condition trend monitoring (ECTM) services as a CAMP Systems Designated Analysis Center (DAC). Precision Air is Tanzania’s premier airline, with a 30+ year legacy of dependable service and warm hospitality. From its hub in Dar es Salaam, Precision Air operates an extensive network that seamlessly links major domestic destinations like Kilimanjaro, Zanzibar, Arusha, Mtwara, Kahama and Mwanza with regional routes to Nairobi and Comoros. More than just an airline, Precision Air is a vital bridge for tourism and business, proudly connecting the world to East Africa’s most iconic national parks, cultural treasures and coastal gems. ### StandardAero is a leading independent pure-play provider of aerospace engine aftermarket services for fixed- and rotary-wing aircraft, serving the commercial, military and business aviation end markets. StandardAero provides a comprehensive suite of critical, value-added aftermarket solutions, including engine maintenance, repair and overhaul, engine component repair, on-wing and field service support, asset management and engineering solutions. StandardAero is an NYSE listed company under the ticker symbol SARO.

(Nasdaq: CARL) (“Carlsmed” or the “Company”), a medical technology company pioneering AI-enabled personalized spine surgery solutions, today reported financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. “Our second quarter 2026 results reflect the growing momentum of aprevo® procedures and further progress on our path to profitability,” said Mike Cordonnier, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. "We delivered 57% revenue growth year-over-year, expanded gross margins by 340 basis points, and grew our trained surgeon user base by more than 60% over the prior year. We continue to see strong volume growth across lumbar and cervical aprevo® procedures, with continued advancements in our proprietary digital production system enabling scalability ahead of strong market demand. We believe the recent CMS ruling – which takes effect on October 1, 2026, and provides new and enhanced hospital reimbursement for the aprevo® lumbar procedure – positions us well for ongoing growth in the years to come." Recent Business Highlights Surgeon adoption grew significantly, with total trained surgeon users up over 60% year-over-year, led by strong engagement from early-career and post-fellowship surgeons CMS Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) rule for fiscal year 2027 recently finalized to include three new MS-DRG codes and favorable reimbursement for inpatient aprevo® lumbar procedures, a significant milestone towards expanding access for Medicare patients aprevo® cervical completed second full quarter of commercialization, now representing approximately 10% of quarterly revenue, with surgeon training on the platform expanding significantly since last quarter Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $74–$78 million, over 50% growth at the midpoint versus full-year 2025, reflecting strong volume trends and a robust pipeline Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Revenue was $18.9 million for the second quarter of 2026, a 57% increase compared to $12.1 million in the second quarter of 2025. Gross profit for the second quarter of 2026 was $14.5 million compared to $8.9 million for the second quarter of 2025. Gross margin was 76.8% for the second quarter of 2026, compared with 73.4% in the second quarter of 2025. Operating expenses were $25.6 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared with $15.4 million for the second quarter of 2025, which consisted of: Research and development expenses of $6.0 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared with $4.2 million for the second quarter of 2025. Sales and marketing expenses of $11.9 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared with $7.9 million for the second quarter of 2025. General and administrative expenses of $7.6 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared with $3.3 million for the second quarter of 2025. Net loss was ($10.5) million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to a ($6.8) million net loss for the second quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was ($8.6) million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to ($6.2) million for the second quarter of 2025. Cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term investments, and marketable securities were $89.3 million as of June 30, 2026. 2026 Financial Outlook Revenue for the full year 2026 is expected to be in the range of $74 to $78 million, representing growth of over 50% at the midpoint of the range over 2025. This compares to prior guidance of $72 to $77 million. A live webcast of the conference call will be available in the Events & Presentations section of the Company’s investor website at investors.carlsmed.com . A replay will be archived on the Company’s website following completion of the call. Non-GAAP Financial Measures This press release contains certain financial information that is not presented in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), including adjusted EBITDA. The non-GAAP financial measures are provided as supplemental information to Carlsmed’s financial measures presented in this press release that are calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP. The Company calculates adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss), as adjusted to exclude, as applicable, (i) net interest income (expense), (ii) income tax expense (benefit), (iii) depreciation expense from property and equipment (iv) amortization expense from long-lived assets, (iv) stock-based compensation expense and (v) change in fair value of warrant liabilities. This non-GAAP measure is presented because management believes it allows investors to view the Company’s performance in a manner similar to the method used by management to evaluate financial performance for both strategic and annual operating planning. Management believes that to properly understand short-term and long-term financial trends, it is helpful for investors to understand the impact of the items excluded from the calculation of adjusted EBITDA, in addition to considering the Company’s GAAP financial measures. The excluded items vary in frequency and/or impact on our results of operations and management believes that the excluded items are not reflective of the Company’s ongoing core business operations and financial condition. Excluding such items allows investors and analysts to compare our operating performance to other companies in our industry and to compare the Company’s period-over-period results. The non-GAAP financial measures used by Carlsmed may not be the same or calculated in the same manner as those used and calculated by other companies. Non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as analytical tools and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for Carlsmed’s financial results prepared and reported in accordance with GAAP. This non-GAAP measure should not be construed as an inference that the Company’s future results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items. We urge investors to review the reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures to the comparable GAAP financial measures included in this press release, and not to rely on any single financial measure to evaluate our business. title: Entergy New Orleans’ Patrick Morel honored nationally for commitment to customers and community
summary: Entergy New Orleans is proud to congratulate Senior Lineworker Patrick Morel for receiving national recognition during the Edison Electric Institute’s National Lineworker Appreciation Day celebration…
body_text: Entergy New Orleans is proud to congratulate Senior Lineworker Patrick Morel for receiving national recognition during the Edison Electric Institute’s National Lineworker Appreciation Day celebration in Washington, D.C. The honor celebrates Morel’s unwavering commitment to safely delivering reliable electric service and reflects the dedication of the skilled lineworkers who serve customers across our community every day. For more numerous years, Morel has helped keep the lights on for customers throughout Entergy New Orleans’ service area. Whether restoring power after severe weather, maintaining critical electric infrastructure or responding to outages, he has built a reputation for professionalism, expertise and a steadfast commitment to service. For Morel, linework is more than a profession. It is a family tradition that inspired his career from an early age. “I inherited a passion for the trade at a very young age. My father has been a lineman for more than 30 years. I always knew that this was the career path I wanted to take,” said Morel. Following in his father’s footsteps gave Morel a deep appreciation for the responsibility that comes with the work. It also instilled the values of discipline, teamwork and service that continue to guide him every day. Those qualities have shaped a career focused on helping customers and the communities we serve. Throughout his career, Morel has supported numerous power restoration efforts, often working long hours under challenging conditions to restore service safely and as quickly as possible. His commitment reflects the dedication shared by Entergy New Orleans’ lineworkers, who stand ready to respond whenever communities are impacted by storms or unexpected outages. For Morel, the greatest reward is knowing that his work makes a meaningful difference in the lives of others. “Being a lineman has given me a strong sense of purpose, knowing that every day I am making a positive impact on the community while providing for my family,” said Morel. Morel’s recognition highlights the professionalism, expertise and dedication demonstrated by lineworkers across the enterprise. Their work strengthens the electric system, restores service during emergencies and helps ensure customers have the reliable power they depend on every day. Entergy New Orleans remains committed to recognizing the exceptional employees who power our communities and proudly congratulates Patrick Morel on this well-deserved national honor.

title: What Türkiye’s Mobile Gaming Ecosystem Can Teach Us
summary: In a recent episode of Tenjin ROI 101, host Tabarak Paracha sat down with Batuhan Avucan, founder of Mobidictum, to discuss how Türkiye's gaming ecosystem developed and whether its success was the result of deliberate design or fortunate timing.
body_text: Many markets produce one breakout company, then spend the next decade asking why it did not happen again.Türkiye’s mobile gaming ecosystem followed a different path. It produced a first generation of successful founders, then a second, and now a third. As Batuhan Avucan , founder of Mobidictum , explained during a recent episode of Tenjin ROI 101 : “The obvious starting point is Peak Games. The success of Peak wasn’t just important for gaming. It was important for the entire startup ecosystem because it was Turkey’s first unicorn.” Peak Games raised approximately $19 million in venture funding before Zynga agreed to acquire the company for $1.8 billion in 2020. For most companies, that would be where the story ends. For Türkiye’s gaming industry, it was where the ecosystem began. [ 1 ][ 2 ] The acquisition helped circulate capital, operating experience, knowledge, and investor confidence throughout the market. Former Peak employees and investors went on to found or support dozens of other companies. By 2022, Startups.watch had traced 65 startups to people whose paths crossed with Peak, including 28 gaming companies. [ 3 ] The wider Turkish gaming ecosystem continued to expand. The latest official ecosystem report counts 757 active studios, 13 incubators, 22 gaming-focused accelerators, and 12 gaming-specific investors. It also ranks Istanbul as Europe’s second-largest gaming hub after London. [ 4 ] By 2025, Dream Games, founded by former Peak executives, generated an estimated $1.7 billion in app-store in-app purchase revenue. Peak Games generated an estimated $619.7 million during the same year. These AppMagic estimates exclude webshops, advertising, and other alternative revenue sources, but they still demonstrate how far the ecosystem’s next generation has grown. [ 5 ] Peak did not simply become Türkiye’s biggest gaming success story. It helped create a system capable of producing more. We sat down with Batuhan to understand how that happened and what other emerging markets can learn from it. In brief: Türkiye’s mobile gaming ecosystem grew through five reinforcing forces: a landmark exit, the circulation of experienced talent, an execution-focused operating culture, resilience under difficult conditions, and a global-first approach to product development. Peak Games provided the proof point, but repeated generations of founders turned one success into an ecosystem. Türkiye’s Mobile Gaming Ecosystem in Numbers Indicator Evidence Peak Games funding before acquisition Approximately $18 million Zynga acquisition of Peak Games $1.8 billion Startups connected to Peak alumni by 2022 65 Peak-connected gaming startups by 2022 28 Active gaming studios in Türkiye 757 Gaming incubators 13 Gaming-focused accelerators 22 Gaming-specific investors 12 Dream Games’ estimated 2025 IAP revenue $1.7 billion Peak Games’ estimated 2025 IAP revenue $619.7 million Revenue figures are AppMagic estimates covering the App Store and Google Play. They do not include advertising, webshops, or other direct-to-consumer revenue. Lesson 1: One Success Can Fuel an Entire Ecosystem Within Türkiye’s startup community, the network of companies created by former Peak employees is sometimes called the “Peak Mafia.” The name references the PayPal Mafia, the group of former PayPal founders and employees who went on to build and fund companies across Silicon Valley. In Türkiye, Peak alumni helped establish companies including Dream Games, Spyke Games, and Ace Games. Batuhan explains the effect: “The key impact of Peak was that it created a generation of founders with exit experience. People who worked there had stock options, experience, and confidence to start their own companies. That’s how the second wave of startups emerged: Dream Games, Spyke, Ace Games, and others.” What the acquisition distributed was not only capital. It distributed first-hand knowledge of how to build, operate, monetize, and scale a globally successful mobile game. That experience reduced uncertainty for the next generation. Employees became founders. Founders became mentors and investors. International investors gained a group of operators whose ability to build global products had already been tested. Dream Games is the clearest example. Its founding team had previously worked together on Toy Blast and Toon Blast at Peak. In March 2021, Dream announced a $50 million Series A on the same day that Royal Match launched globally, bringing its total funding to $57.5 million. [ 6 ] Investors were not evaluating an unknown team in a vacuum. They were backing founders whose previous work had contributed to a $1.8 billion acquisition. That is the real mechanism behind the idea that one success produces another. It is not only inspiration. It is underwriting. Lesson 2: Iteration Can Be a Competitive Advantage Batuhan describes a pattern shared by many successful Turkish mobile gaming studios: they do not always begin by attempting to invent an entirely new category. Instead, they take a proven model and focus on executing it more effectively through stronger monetization, sharper live operations, faster development cycles, and constant product iteration. “You don’t have to disrupt anything. You just need to make something a little bit better, a little bit easier, or different. But now the market is starting to change. AI has accelerated development, competition is completely global, and new regions like Vietnam are also catching up very quickly.” Mobile gaming rewards teams that can measure player behavior, understand retention, improve conversion, and respond quickly to performance data. Within that environment, iteration is not necessarily a lack of ambition. It is a disciplined way to reduce product risk. A team can begin with a format players already understand, then compete through execution, polish, live operations, user acquisition, and monetization. That approach becomes more powerful when knowledge moves between companies. Each generation does not have to learn every lesson from the beginning. New studios inherit operating standards, hiring networks, investor relationships, and an understanding of the metrics required to compete globally. The strategic question now is whether Türkiye’s execution advantage can also produce more original intellectual property, game formats, and entertainment brands. Batuhan puts the question directly: “Do we still rely only on iteration, or is it time for something more innovative?” The answer may define the ecosystem’s next stage. Lesson 3: Resilience Matters When Capital Is Not Enough Türkiye’s government incentive programs and growing venture capital ecosystem have helped gaming companies manage costs and scale their operations. Batuhan describes the incentives as a type of reimbursement system: “It works like a cashback system. You spend money and later get part of it back. That improves cash flow, especially for marketing. However, payments can take a long time, sometimes up to a year, and currency fluctuations reduce the real value. So yes, it helps, but the real driver is still VC funding, talent, and execution.” The distinction matters. Incentives can extend a company’s runway or help it invest more aggressively in marketing and tools. They cannot create product-market fit, build an effective team, or guarantee that players will stay. Batuhan believes the harder-to-measure factor is resilience: “Resilience is the factor that sets Turkish founders apart. They don’t give up easily. They don’t blame the market. Many companies struggled for years before succeeding. Some founders almost quit multiple times. But they persisted. That’s the main pattern, not background, not funding, but persistence.” That does not mean capital is unimportant. Modern mobile gaming requires serious investment in product development, user acquisition, live operations, and measurement. It means that capital and incentives act as multipliers. Their value depends on the team applying them. Studios operating in the same market may have access to similar programs, investors, and talent. What separates them is often how quickly they learn, how effectively they respond when a product underperforms, and whether they continue building when the first approach fails. Lesson 4: A Mature Ecosystem Produces More Diversity The conditions that supported the rapid growth of hypercasual gaming through 2021 have changed. Competition is more global, user acquisition is more expensive, and the level of product quality required to break through has increased. As a result, founders are beginning to apply their experience outside traditional mobile gaming. Batuhan explains: “Mobile gaming requires serious planning, metrics, and funding. At the same time, mobile apps are becoming more attractive, with companies like Codeway and others scaling well without gaming risk. So founders are diversifying into apps, PC gaming, or other tech sectors.” Companies such as Codeway, HubX, and AppNation demonstrate how Türkiye’s mobile product expertise can be applied to non-gaming categories. Other founders are moving toward PC gaming, where the development, distribution, and monetization models differ considerably. Batuhan describes the distinction this way: “Mobile gaming is very different from PC gaming. Mobile gaming is more like mathematics, focused on metrics like conversion rates, retention, and optimization. PC gaming is more about creative experience.” This diversification is not necessarily evidence that Türkiye’s mobile gaming ecosystem is weakening. It may be evidence that it has matured. The underlying skills developed inside gaming, including user acquisition, monetization, experimentation, creative testing, data analysis, and global distribution, can transfer into adjacent categories. A healthy ecosystem does not need every new founder to recreate the same company. It needs experienced people to keep building, even when they choose a different market. Lesson 5: Build for a Global Market from Day One Mobile products are not constrained by the size of their domestic market in the same way as many traditional businesses. Turkish studios learned to take advantage of that early. Rather than proving a product locally and expanding later, many build for international audiences from the beginning. “Most Turkish companies don’t actually test in Turkey and then scale. They usually go straight to the US market. The US is often the real testing ground.” This global-first approach influences more than distribution. It affects product design, monetization, pricing, user acquisition, creative strategy, performance measurement, and the benchmarks teams use to judge success. A studio based entirely in Istanbul can compete for the same players as companies in London, Helsinki, San Francisco, Seoul, or Ho Chi Minh City. Its physical location does not prevent it from reaching global app-store charts. That opportunity also increases the level of competition. Turkish studios are not only competing against one another. They are competing against the best-funded and most experienced teams in the world. The ecosystem’s response has been to treat global reach as the starting condition, not a later stage of growth. Lessons for the Turkish Mobile Gaming Ecosystem Türkiye’s mobile gaming ecosystem was not created by one company, one government program, or one moment. Peak Games provided the proof point. The ecosystem grew because the value created by that success continued to circulate. Those former employees became founders. Experienced founders became investors and mentors. International capital entered the market. New studios inherited operating knowledge from the companies that came before them. Each generation began with a stronger foundation than the last. That is the broader lesson for markets trying to produce their own technology ecosystems. A breakout company matters most when its experience spreads beyond the company itself. The goal should not simply be to manufacture one unicorn. It should be to create the conditions through which one success can make many others more likely. Türkiye’s next generation may not follow Peak’s path exactly, especially since mbile gaming has become more competitive, and founders are already moving into PC games, mobile apps, entertainment, and other technology categories. This diversification may be a sign of strength: the ecosystem is no longer dependent on producing the next Peak Games, nor the same format. Looking ahead, Batuhan expects more unicorns, consolidation, and major exits. His greater hope is that Turkish companies begin thinking beyond short-term outcomes and build enduring global businesses that can expand across games, media, entertainment, and entirely new categories. This would be the clearest sign that the ecosystem has fully evolved: not simply producing successful studios, but producing generations of founders who know how to build, adapt, and compete globally. Peak Games proved that a global gaming company could be built from Istanbul. The companies that followed proved it could happen again. Frequently Asked Questions Why is Türkiye successful in mobile gaming? Türkiye combines an experienced talent pool, a strong culture of execution and iteration, access to domestic and international investment, government support programs, and a global-first approach to product development. Peak Games also created a major proof point that increased investor confidence and produced a generation of experienced founders. What impact did Peak Games have on Türkiye’s startup ecosystem? Peak Games became Türkiye’s first billion-dollar startup when Zynga agreed to acquire it for $1.8 billion in 2020. Its employees, founders, and investors later helped establish and fund dozens of other companies, spreading capital and operating experience across the ecosystem. Which gaming companies were founded by Peak Games alumni? Well-known examples include Dream Games, Spyke Games, and Ace Games. Startups.watch reported in 2022 that people connected to Peak had founded 65 startups across different sectors, including 28 gaming companies. How many game studios are there in Türkiye? The State of Turkish Startup Ecosystem 2025 report counted 757 active gaming studios. It also reported 13 incubators, 22 gaming-focused accelerators, and 12 gaming-specific investors. What role do government incentives play in Türkiye’s gaming industry? Government incentives can reimburse eligible costs and improve cash flow for studios investing in areas such as marketing and tools. However, Batuhan argues that incentives work best as a multiplier for teams that already have talent, funding, and strong execution. Is Türkiye’s technology ecosystem expanding beyond mobile games? Yes. Founders and operators are increasingly applying their experience to PC games, non-gaming mobile apps, and other technology categories. This suggests that knowledge developed within mobile gaming is spreading into the wider Turkish startup ecosystem. title: Where to Watch Scars on the Mountain
summary: Scars on the Mountain tells the inspiring true story of a North Carolina community devastated by Hurricane Helene and the extraordinary people who found hope...
body_text: < Back Where to Watch Scars on the Mountain by Angel | August 4, 2026 In just a matter of hours, Hurricane Helene transformed a quiet Appalachian community into the center of one of the most devastating natural disasters in recent memory. Scars on the Mountain is a moving documentary that captures the heartbreak, resilience, and hope that emerged when neighbors became each other’s lifeline. Stream Scars on the Mountain now on Angel. What Is Scars on the Mountain About When Hurricane Helene made landfall, most people assumed the worst of it would be felt along the coast. Instead, the storm pushed 300 miles inland and came down on Yancey County, North Carolina—a small Appalachian community tucked into the mountains—with a force no one had prepared for. Record-breaking flash floods and landslides tore through the area within hours. Roads washed out, power lines went down, and communication cut off entirely. With no way in and no way out, the people of Yancey County were left to face the aftermath alone. Scars on the Mountain documents what happened in the days and weeks that followed: the chaos, the loss, and the quiet, remarkable ways neighbors showed up for each other when every outside system had failed them. Why This Documentary Is Worth Your Time Scars on the Mountain doesn’t focus on the storm itself as much as the people who lived through it. Through firsthand stories, it captures what happened after the floodwaters receded. It’s also a reminder that some of the most meaningful acts of courage aren’t found in headlines. They’re found in ordinary people checking on neighbors, sharing what little they have, and refusing to let one another face hardship alone. Whether you followed the aftermath of Hurricane Helene or are learning about it for the first time, Scars on the Mountain offers an honest look at a community that endured the unthinkable—and the hope that emerged in the middle of it. Where To Watch Scars on the Mountain Whether you experienced Hurricane Helene firsthand or are discovering this story for the first time, Scars on the Mountain offers a powerful reminder of what people are capable of when they come together to care for one another. It’s the kind of documentary that stays with you long after it ends. Watch Scars on the Mountain now on Angel. --- Streaming availability may vary by region. title: Clarivate Enhances SkyRiver to Help Libraries Share, Reuse and Create Trusted Metadata
summary: Combining community metadata sharing, institutional choice and AI-powered record creation
body_text: Combining community metadata sharing, institutional choice and AI-powered record creation LONDON, UK, August 12, 2026 – Clarivate Plc (NYSE: CLVT), a leading global provider of transformative intelligence, today announced the launch of the enhanced SkyRiver platform, designed to give libraries an affordable way to source, manage and share open bibliographic metadata while supporting interoperability across institutions, consortia and library management systems. Using open metadata by default, SkyRiver makes records as reusable as possible while respecting contributor requirements, licensing obligations and institutional governance policies. Libraries retain institutional choice over participation and contribution. Libraries today face growing pressure to increase efficiency and adapt discovery services. Trusted, transparent and interoperable metadata provides an important foundation for responsible discovery. To support this, the enhanced SkyRiver platform introduces AI-powered record creation capabilities to create metadata more efficiently. Yoel Goldenberg, Senior Vice President, Product Management, Academia & Government at Clarivate, said: “Libraries need trusted metadata that can be shared, reused and integrated across systems without sacrificing choice, transparency or governance. “The enhanced SkyRiver platform helps libraries work more efficiently through community open metadata sharing, while introducing AI-powered capabilities that make it easier to create high-quality records. As libraries explore the future of discovery, trusted metadata will be more important than ever.” Trevor A. Dawes, Vice Provost for Libraries and Museums and May Morris University Librarian, University of Delaware, said: “Our partnership with Clarivate on SkyRiver reflects our commitment to high-quality, open metadata that increases the visibility and discoverability of our collections while supporting collaboration across the library community.” Brett Waytuck, Dean, University Libraries and Archives, University of Regina, said: “Discoverability depends on trusted metadata and workflows that recognise the value libraries contribute. The enhanced SkyRiver platform presents an opportunity to explore a practical approach that preserves local metadata enhancements, integrates with existing operations and helps libraries realise greater value from their collections.” The enhanced SkyRiver platform helps libraries: Access trusted metadata that supports discovery, cataloguing and resource sharing Connect, exchange and reuse metadata across library management systems Enable interoperability across institutions, consortia and library networks Retain institutional choice and governance over participation and contribution Access clear information on rights, source, attribution and access Benefit from AI-enabled record creation capabilities that support efficient metadata workflows Reuse open bibliographic metadata while respecting contributor and licensing requirements As part of its ongoing commitment to transparency and community engagement, Clarivate plans to establish a Metadata Governance Advisory Group to help guide future development of the platform and provide input on metadata policy, quality standards and governance principles. Learn more about SkyRiver at https://iii.com/products/skyriver . About Clarivate Clarivate is a leading global provider of transformative intelligence. We offer enriched data, insights & analytics, workflow solutions and expert services in the areas of Academia & Government, Intellectual Property and Life Sciences & Healthcare. For more information, please visit www.clarivate.com Media contact: Amy Bourke-Waite newsroom@clarivate.com content_copy Copy link Copied

title: InQuery Joins InsurTech NY's 2026 Match Program
summary: InQuery is one of 10 companies in InsurTech NY's 2026 Match Program, connecting insurtechs with carriers, brokers, and investors across claims and legal work.
body_text: InQuery has been selected as one of 10 companies participating in InsurTech NY’s 2026 Match Program. Your browser does not support embedded videos. Watch the announcement instead. 1 of 10 companies selected for the 2026 Match Program cohort InsurTech NY pairs growth-stage insurtechs with carriers, brokers, and investors. The program connects growth-stage insurtech companies with carriers, brokers, investors, and industry leaders to help accelerate commercial partnerships and bring new technology into real insurance workflows. For InQuery, the timing is especially relevant as we continue expanding our work at the intersection of claims and legal operations. One file, two teams reading it apart Many of the most expensive claims eventually become legal problems. Once counsel gets involved, the underlying file can include thousands of pages of medical records, bills, demand packages , expert reports, correspondence, and litigation documents. Adjusters and attorneys are often working from the same underlying evidence, but reconstructing the story separately for different decisions. That creates a lot of friction. Turning the file into a factual record InQuery helps turn those large, unstructured files into a clearer factual record. We organize medical records , build chronologies , analyze bills and demand packages, identify documentation gaps , and surface the facts that matter for claim evaluation and litigation strategy. The goal is not to replace the judgment of an adjuster or attorney. It is to make sure that judgment starts from a cleaner, more complete understanding of the file. That becomes especially important when teams are deciding: How to respond to a demand Whether a claim needs to be escalated What information should be sent to defense counsel Whether additional records and expert review are needed before a decision is made What we’re hoping to learn Through the Match Program, we’re looking forward to spending more time with carriers and claims leaders to understand where legal and claims workflows still break down, and where AI can help teams get to the right information earlier. We’re grateful to InsurTech NY for including InQuery in this year’s cohort and excited to keep building. Work with InQuery Explore our services
